some ships just cant be raised with ropes. rope breaks after a certain ammount of tries, as well as the skill, but as you level up the skill, youre more likely to get the ship before it breaks.

comments.author: Lancelot
comments.body: You *cannot* drop and raise the ship to gain proficiency. You do not get any proficiency from re-raising the ship (tested and confirmed by me), and I heard (unconfirmed) that the loot is worse if you let it sink.

comments.author: Misun

if u drop the wreck before u "FIRST" success salvaging (let say at 90%), doing salvage again will give u skill prof

if u drop the wreck after u already salvaged it, u wont get any exp from potential re-salvage

comments.author: Edgedemon
comments.body:
the +1 does help with raising high difficulty Shipwrecks, but consider that worse case scenario you would just have to try to raise it again, this can still be important with Arctic Shipwrecks, Haul however can be circumvented altogether, if you get a ship with Haul Assist skill (Cruise Galleon / Endeavor / San Gabriel or inherited ) you do not need to even have the Haul skill to salvage your haul would never be interrupted.

even if you do choose to have haul skill you definitely can do without the +1 haul on aide

comments.author: Nekos
comments.body:
If you want to raise the ship fast, pick up a ship with > 80 people, like a caravel or galley.

If you want to squeeze the sink ships, the raising has to be slow. Meaning around 50 people , durability at least 400, and repair skill.

You need certain amount of people because raising the ship will make people will fall from your ship.

Raising the ship fast i did get around 60 proficiency points, raising it slow i get around 140.
